notes: Full description: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs CrlChecker::with_delta() at lines 153-158. The function calls base_crl_number(&delta_crl) which returns None if the deltaCRLIndicator extension is absent OR if its INTEGER value cannot be decoded. Then line 155: 'if delta_base_num.is_none() { return Err(Error::DeltaCrlBaseMismatch); }' with comment 'No deltaCRLIndicator -> this is not a delta CRL.' But if has_delta_crl_indicator() returns true (extension present) and base_crl_number() returns None (value malformed), the error is still DeltaCrlBaseMismatch, which is misleading — the actual error is a parse failure. The code is fail-closed (rejects malformed delta CRL), but the error type is wrong. The function checks has_delta_crl_indicator(base_crl) first to ensure the BASE is not a delta, but the same has_delta_crl_indicator check is not done before the delta_base_num check to distinguish 'absent extension' from 'present but malformed value'. Fix: Call has_delta_crl_indicator(&delta_crl) before base_crl_number(). If has_delta_crl_indicator returns true but base_crl_number returns None, return Err(Error::CrlParseError(...)) or a new Error::DeltaCrlMalformed variant. If has_delta_crl_indicator returns false, return DeltaCrlBaseMismatch. Priority: P2 (diagnostic clarity — wrong error type confuses callers).
title: FINDING: with_delta() conflates malformed deltaCRLIndicator with missing indicator
